result.title: Why Wildfires Are Increasing & In-demand Employment Skills | WEF | Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:12 - In-demand skills employers struggle to find:
Core practical abilities - in construction, operation and resources handling - account for almost half of #employment worldwide. But demand is running way ahead of supply, which means in many regions there’s a shortage of people with these skills. In the US, people with maker skills are doing five times as much overtime as other workers, on average.

02:07 -Why are wildfires increasing?:
Wildfires have devastated landscapes across the world this year, from France and Spain to Southeast Asia. What’s driving the fires? A combination of extreme heat, wind and dryness, exacerbated both by climate change and the failure to prepare - as Natalie Çilem of the World Economic Forum’s Global Network for Wildfire Leadership explains.

04:56 - Top 10 tourism destinations:
Every two years, the World Economic Forum ranks countries as traveller destinations - not using simple visitor numbers, but against a set of indicators showing their ‘tourism readiness’. These include the quality of roads and the number of hotel rooms to the sustainability of its tourism infrastructure and the quality of natural and cultural attractions. This year’s Travel and Tourism Development Index has a new leader. Can you guess which country it is?

result.title: Employers can’t find enough workers with these skills
result.description:
‘Maker skills’ are the engine of the global economy. 

These core practical abilities - in construction, operation and resources handling - account for almost half of #employment worldwide. 

But demand is running way ahead of supply, which means in many regions there’s a shortage of people with these skills. In the US, people with maker skills are doing five times as much overtime as other workers, on average.

A new report examines the reasons behind the shortage of makers and offers five major recommendations for how to grow the maker workforce of tomorrow. Read it here: https://www.weforum.org/publications/new-economy-skills-skills-for-the-maker-economy/

result.title: The body’s built-in courier
result.description:
One of the most promising new medical technologies is a natural drug delivery system that could help beat Alzheimer's and other diseases that have been hard to treat for decades.

It relies on exosomes, tiny messenger bubbles created by cells. Kimmy Bettinger explains to Robin Pomeroy how exosomes work.

Watch the full episode on the Top 10 Emerging Technologies 2026 here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2H4pXNZldHs&t=1s

result.title: World Economic Forum’s Chief Economists Outlook: September 2026
result.description:
Chief Economists Outlook

The global economy continues to navigate a period of significant disruption, with ongoing conflicts in multiple regions, volatile bond markets and growing debate over the infrastructure, technologies and investments that could shape the future.

How are companies adapting to these shifts and what trends are leading economists watching most closely?

Speakers:
Saadia Zahidi, Managing Director, World Economic Forum
Nela Richardson, Chief Economist and Environmental, Social and Governance Officer, ADP
Ufuk Akcigit, Deputy Chief Economist and Director of Private Markets, World Bank Group
Svenja Gudell, Chief Economist, Indeed
